title: WiseOwl COBOL source listing, schema version 1.0
description: The source listing of one compilation: the source as read, with its COPY inclusions and programs. Lines are referred to by their listing line number and files by their id. Every format (text, JSON) renders this one document.

$schema.description: The identifier of the schema the document follows: urn:wiseowl:cobol:listing:v1 for every version of major 1.

schemaVersion.description: The schema version the document was written at, <major>.<minor>. A reader of major 1 reads every 1.x document and ignores the properties it does not know.

header.description: The compiler, the edition, the compilation timestamp, the main source and the outcome.

edition.description: The edition's year as --std spells it (85, 2002, 2014, 2023).

compiledAt.description: The compilation's one instant (DESIGN-listing.md section 5): the same instant WHEN-COMPILED and DATE-COMPILED's replacement denote.

mainSource.description: The path of the source file compiled.

outcome.description: How far the compilation got. Success: The assembly was written. FrontendError: The text stages or the parser refused the source. BindError: The binder refused the program. BackendError: The backend could not produce the assembly. OutputNotWritable: The source compiled, but the host refused to write the assembly.

parse.description: Whether the source was parsed, and whether the parse had to recover from a syntax error: the program map and the statistics' programs, statements and verbs are read off the parse, so after a recovery they hold only what the recovery kept. NotParsed: The source was not parsed: the text stages refused it. Parsed: The parse read the whole source with no syntax error. Recovered: The parse recovered from a syntax error and may have skipped source: a program, statement or verb the recovery skipped is missing from the program map and the statistics.

files.description: Every file read: the source and each library text.

items.description: One file the compilation read.

path.description: The path as the compilation read it.

role.description: Source or library text. Source: The source file the compilation was asked to compile. Library: A library text a COPY statement read.

sha256.description: The lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the file's bytes as read.

inclusions.description: Every COPY statement processed, in text order.

items.description: One COPY statement and the library text it brought in.

parent.description: The inclusion whose library text holds the COPY statement, or null for the source.

depth.description: 1 for a COPY statement of the source, one more per library text it is nested in.

copyLine.description: The listing line the COPY word stands on.

copyLastLine.description: The listing line the statement ends on; the inclusion's lines follow it.

textName.description: The text-name or literal the statement names.

libraryName.description: The library-name or literal of its OF / IN phrase, or null.

file.description: The Id of the library text read, or null when none was.

outcome.description: Found, not found or circular. Found: The library text was found and copied. NotFound: No library text of that name was found; nothing was copied. Circular: The library text copies itself, directly or through others; it was not copied again.

suppress.description: The statement writes the SUPPRESS phrase: the library text it incorporates is not listed, and the statement itself is (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR4).

lines.description: The source section, in listing order: every physical line of every file read, each inclusion's lines after the last line of its COPY statement.

items.description: One physical line of the source section (DESIGN-listing.md section 4.2).

number.description: The listing line number, 1-based, unique in the document.

file.description: The Id the line is read from.

fileLine.description: The 1-based physical line of that file.

inclusion.description: The Id the line belongs to; null for the source.

depth.description: The inclusion depth, 0 for the source.

form.description: Fixed or free form. Fixed: Fixed-form reference format: sequence area, indicator area, areas A and B, identification area. Free: Free-form reference format.

kind.description: What the line is. Source: A line of program text. Comment: A comment line: the fixed-form * indicator, or the floating comment indicator. PageEjectComment: A comment line with the fixed-form slant (/) indicator, which ejects a page before it is listed. DebuggingLine: A debugging line: the fixed-form D indicator, or the floating >>D indicator. Continuation: A fixed-form continuation line (the hyphen indicator). Directive: A compiler directive line, where the edition has compiler directives. CommentEntry: A line of the comment-entry of an IDENTIFICATION DIVISION paragraph such as AUTHOR or DATE-COMPILED. CcvsExcluded: A line the NIST CCVS column-7 conventions exclude (the --nist dialect only). NotAnIndicator: A line whose indicator area holds a character that is no indicator, read as program text. Blank: A blank line: nothing but spaces in its program text.

text.description: The physical text as the file holds it, tabs expanded.

omitted.description: A false conditional-compilation branch omitted the line.

listed.description: The visibility pass's answer: the text renderer prints it.

pageBreakBefore.description: The visibility pass's answer: a page starts before it.

program.description: The Id of the innermost program containing the line.

replacement.description: Which replacement the compiler made of the line, if any. None: The line was compiled as written. DateCompiled: The first line of a DATE-COMPILED paragraph, whose paragraph "is replaced during compilation with a paragraph of the form" DATE-COMPILED. current date. (§1985:VI.3.4.4 GR1): the listing prints the replacement in its place. DateCompiledEntry: A further line of the comment-entry of a replaced DATE-COMPILED paragraph: replaced with the paragraph, so the text listing does not print it (the model keeps the written text). Replacing: A replacing action of a REPLACE statement or of a COPY statement's REPLACING phrase matched text that begins on the line, so what was compiled is not what was written: the text listing prints the line as written, marked 'R', and under it the compiled text.

replaced.description: What the compiler compiled in place of Text: DATE-COMPILED's replacement, printed in its place; or, for a line a replacing action changed, the resultant text compiled from it (one line of text per resultant line, joined by line feeds; empty when the replacement removed everything the line held), printed under it.

diagnostics.description: The Id of each diagnostic placed on the line, in listing order.

margin.description: What the text listing prints in the line's margin: on a line that declares a data item, what the data map says of it (its offset, length and usage); on a line that writes references, the listing lines that define the names it uses (the cross-reference); null when the line has neither or the section that says it was not asked for.

item.description: The Id of the data item the line declares (the first, when it declares several), or null on a line that declares none.

definitions.description: On a line that declares no data item, the listing line of the definition of each name the line's references use (the cross-reference), each once, in the order the names are written; empty on a definition line.

names.description: Each reference written on the line, in column order (the cross-reference's references placed on it, its definitions aside): the HTML listing links each to its definition; empty when the cross-reference was not asked for.

items.description: One name written on a source line (DESIGN-listing.md section 4.2): the join of the cross-reference onto the line, made once, which the HTML listing links to the name's definition.

column.description: The 1-based character position of its first character in the line's text.

length.description: The characters it is written in on this line.

use.description: How it uses the name. Defined: The declaration. Read: A reference at no position its statement stores into. Written: A reference at a position its statement stores into, wholly or in part. Modified: A reference at a position its statement reads and stores into (ADD TO, SUBTRACT FROM, INSPECT REPLACING, a STRING POINTER, ...).

spans.description: What the compiler read each stretch of Text as, in column order and never overlapping: its reference-format areas, comments, words, literals, picture character-strings and separators, at the edition in force. The HTML listing colours the text by them; text no span covers (spaces, a line no stage read) has no class.

items.description: One classified stretch of a listing line's text (DESIGN-listing.md section 7.2; kb/Work PB5949).

column.description: The 1-based character position in the line's text (Text, tabs expanded) of its first character.

class.description: What the compiler read the stretch as. SequenceArea: The sequence number area of a fixed-form line, positions 1 to 6. Indicator: The indicator area of a fixed-form line, position 7, when it holds an indicator. IdentificationArea: The text of a fixed-form line past margin R, which the compiler ignores (the identification area). Comment: A comment: the text of a comment line, an inline comment, or a debugging line read as a comment. CommentEntry: A comment-entry of an identification division paragraph. Directive: A compiler directive line. ReservedWord: A reserved word of the edition in force. ContextWord: A word read as a keyword that the edition in force does not reserve: a context-sensitive word in its context, a word a general format recognizes by its spelling, or a later edition's keyword. FunctionName: An intrinsic-function-name or the function-name a FUNCTION reference names. UserWord: A user-defined word or a system-name: a word read as a name. LevelNumber: A level-number. AlphanumericLiteral: An alphanumeric literal, hexadecimal ones included. NationalLiteral: A national literal. BooleanLiteral: A boolean literal. NumericLiteral: A numeric literal. FigurativeConstant: A figurative constant, and the ALL that prefixes one. Picture: A picture character-string. Separator: A separator other than the space: the period, comma, semicolon, parentheses and colon. Operator: An arithmetic, relational, concatenation or invocation operator. EmbeddedText: The text of an embedded precompiler block (EXEC ... END-EXEC). Unrecognized: A character no lexical rule reads, which the compiler reports.

programs.description: Every source unit, in text order, with its nesting and listing line range.

items.description: One source unit of the compilation group (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.5).

name.description: The name its identification paragraph declares, as written.

kind.description: Program, function, class, ... Program: A program. Function: A user-defined function. Class: A class definition. Interface: An interface definition. Factory: The factory definition of a class. Object: The object (instance) definition of a class. Method: A method definition.

parent.description: The Id of the unit that directly contains it, or null.

firstLine.description: The first listing line of the unit.

lastLine.description: The last listing line of the unit.

attributes.description: What the compiler decided for a program or function it bound (its COMMON, INITIAL, RECURSIVE and PROTOTYPE attributes, its externalized name and its .NET type), from the symbol table: null when the bind did not finish, when neither the program map nor the data map was asked for, and for a class, interface, factory, object or method.

externalizedName.description: The name externalized to the operating environment: the AS phrase's literal, else the name.

diagnostics.description: Every diagnostic the compilation reported of its source, in listing order: those placed on a line by line and column, then those placed on none in the order they were reported.

items.description: One diagnostic of the compilation (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.3), placed on the listing line it names.

severity.description: Error, warning or information. Error: An error: the compilation fails. Warning: A warning: the compilation does not fail. Info: Information.

message.description: The diagnostic's text, which names the rule of the edition in force where it cites one.

line.description: The listing line the diagnostic is placed on, or null when it names no place in a file the listing lists (a diagnostic about the compilation as a whole, or about text the compiler generated).

file.description: The Id of the file it names, or null when Line is.

fileLine.description: The 1-based physical line of that file, or null when Line is.

column.description: The 1-based character position in that line's text (Text, tabs expanded), or null when Line is.

citations.description: Each citation of the standard the message makes, in the order written.

items.description: One citation of a COBOL standard a diagnostic's message makes, in the repository's citation format §<edition>:<locator>[ <rule>] (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR14, §1985:VI.5.3.4 GR3).

edition.description: The edition's year as the format writes it: 2023, 2014, 2002 or 1985 for the standards, 1989 and 1993 for the two amendments of the 1985 standard.

locator.description: The clause, or for 1985 the Roman section and paragraph (VI.5.3.4) or printed page (p.VI-20).

rule.description: The rule within the clause (GR1, SR14, RV3, Format 10), or null when none is named.

flag.description: The edition flag the diagnostic is (an obsolete or removed construct, a nonstandard extension in use), as the compiler raised it; null for any other diagnostic.

kind.description: Obsolete, removed or extension. Obsolete: The construct is obsolete or archaic in the edition compiled to: still conforming, flagged by a warning (COBOL0903). Removed: The edition compiled to removed the construct: an error, or under --permissive a warning that keeps the meaning the construct had before (COBOL0902, or the code its construct pins). Extension: The construct is a nonstandard extension the compiler accepts, flagged under --flag-extensions (COBOL2894).

construct.description: The identifier of the construct in the compiler's register of constructs or of nonstandard extensions (exit-program-archaic-2023, usage-comp-3).

description.description: The construct as a user would name it.

edition.description: The edition, as --std spells its year (85, 2002, 2014, 2023), that made the construct obsolete or removed it; for an extension, the edition compiled to, whose standard does not define it.

flaggedConstructs.description: The diagnostics section's table of flagged constructs by edition (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.11): one entry per construct an edition flag of Diagnostics names (Flag), by edition, kind and construct; empty when no diagnostic is an edition flag or the diagnostics section was not asked for.

items.description: One row of the table of flagged constructs by edition (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.11): a construct, the edition and kind of its flag, and every diagnostic that flags it.

kind.description: Obsolete, removed or extension. Obsolete: The construct is obsolete or archaic in the edition compiled to: still conforming, flagged by a warning (COBOL0903). Removed: The edition compiled to removed the construct: an error, or under --permissive a warning that keeps the meaning the construct had before (COBOL0902, or the code its construct pins). Extension: The construct is a nonstandard extension the compiler accepts, flagged under --flag-extensions (COBOL2894).

description.description: The construct as a user would name it.

diagnostics.description: The Id of each diagnostic that flags the construct, in listing order; their number is the construct's count.

displays.description: Every transfer of a DISPLAY directive to the listing, in the order the directives were processed.

items.description: One transfer of a DISPLAY directive to the listing (§2023:7.3.12.4 GR1, GR5 a), GR6; DESIGN-listing.md section 6.10): printed at its directive's place whether or not a LISTING directive suppresses that line (GR2).

line.description: The listing line of the DISPLAY directive.

text.description: The data transferred: each operand's image, in the order written, separated by one space.

options.description: The options section: every option of the compilation with its value and whether it is the default, then the compiler and the host it ran on; empty when the section was not asked for.

items.description: One row of the options section (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.4).

name.description: The option as the command line spells it (--std), or the name of the fact (source, compiler).

value.description: Its value, as the command line spells it where it has a spelling; for a default that is derived from another value (the output path), the value derived.

origin.description: Default, specified, or a fact of the compiler or the host. Default: An option the compilation was not given a value for: its default. Specified: An option given a value other than its default. Host: No option: a fact of the compiler or of the host the compilation ran on (a version, the operating system).

statistics.description: The statistics section: lines by kind and by file, programs, statements, diagnostics by severity and the verbs; null when the section was not asked for.

lines.description: Every line of the listing, counted.

kinds.description: The lines of each kind, every kind once, in the order of ListingLineKind.

items.description: The lines of one kind.

kind.description: The kind. Source: A line of program text. Comment: A comment line: the fixed-form * indicator, or the floating comment indicator. PageEjectComment: A comment line with the fixed-form slant (/) indicator, which ejects a page before it is listed. DebuggingLine: A debugging line: the fixed-form D indicator, or the floating >>D indicator. Continuation: A fixed-form continuation line (the hyphen indicator). Directive: A compiler directive line, where the edition has compiler directives. CommentEntry: A line of the comment-entry of an IDENTIFICATION DIVISION paragraph such as AUTHOR or DATE-COMPILED. CcvsExcluded: A line the NIST CCVS column-7 conventions exclude (the --nist dialect only). NotAnIndicator: A line whose indicator area holds a character that is no indicator, read as program text. Blank: A blank line: nothing but spaces in its program text.

omitted.description: The lines a false conditional-compilation branch omitted (Omitted).

copied.description: The lines of library text a COPY statement copied (Inclusion set).

unlisted.description: The lines the source section does not print (Listed false): a LISTING directive or COPY SUPPRESS suppressed them.

files.description: The lines of each file read, counted, in the order of the files: a library text copied twice counts each copy.

items.description: The lines of one file.

lines.description: Its lines, counted: each listing line read from the file, so each inclusion of a library text counts.

kinds.description: The lines of each kind, every kind once, in the order of ListingLineKind.

omitted.description: The lines a false conditional-compilation branch omitted (Omitted).

copied.description: The lines of library text a COPY statement copied (Inclusion set).

unlisted.description: The lines the source section does not print (Listed false): a LISTING directive or COPY SUPPRESS suppressed them.

diagnostics.description: The diagnostics the compilation reported, counted by severity, every severity once.

items.description: The diagnostics of one severity.

severity.description: The severity. Error: An error: the compilation fails. Warning: A warning: the compilation does not fail. Info: Information.

parse.description: The programs, statements and verbs the parse read, or null when the source was not parsed. After a parse that recovered from a syntax error (the header's parse is Recovered) they are only those the recovery kept.

programs.description: The source units of the program map (Programs).

statements.description: The statements, a statement nested in another counted as well.

verbs.description: Each verb, by the word that begins its statements, in the ordinal order of that word.

items.description: One verb of the verb counts (IBM's VBREF).

verb.description: The word that begins the statements, in upper case (MOVE, GO, NEXT).

lines.description: The listing line each of those statements begins on, in listing order, one entry per statement (a line that begins two of them appears twice); a statement on no line the listing holds has none.

dataMap.description: The data map and the file map: every name of the data division with what the compiler decided for it; null when the section was not asked for or could not be produced.

items.description: Every data description entry, condition-name, index-name, constant-name, report-name and cd-name of every program, class, method and interface, in the order written: FILLER entries, INDEXED BY index-names, named CAPACITY registers, constants, type declarations, level-66 and level-88 entries, the report group description entries of each report and the implicit description of each CD's record area included.
One name of the data map (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.6).

kind.description: Data, condition, index, constant, report or cd. Data: A data description entry (a data-name or FILLER), a level-66 RENAMES entry included. Condition: A condition-name (a level-88 entry). Index: An index-name an INDEXED BY phrase declares. Constant: A constant-name a constant entry declares. Report: A report-name a report description entry (an RD entry) declares; its report group description entries follow it as Data entries of the REPORT section. CommunicationDescription: A cd-name a communication description entry (a CD entry) declares; the implicit description of its record area and the records written after it follow it as Data entries of the COMMUNICATION section that it owns.

name.description: The name as written, or FILLER.

program.description: The Id of the program that declares it, or null when its line is not listed in any program.

line.description: The listing line it is declared on, or null when the listing holds no line for it.

column.description: The 1-based character position of the declaration in that line's text, or null with Line.

level.description: The level-number of a data description entry (66 for a RENAMES entry) or of a report group description entry, 88 for a condition-name; null for an index-name, a constant-name, a report-name or a cd-name.

owner.description: The Id of the group a data item is subordinate to, of a condition-name's conditional variable, of the table whose INDEXED BY phrase declares an index-name, of the report a level-1 report group description entry describes, or of the CD whose record area or record a level-1 entry describes; null for any other level 1, 66 or 77 item, a constant, a report-name and a cd-name.

section.description: The data division section that describes a data item, a report-name or a cd-name: FILE, WORKING-STORAGE, LOCAL-STORAGE, LINKAGE, COMMUNICATION, REPORT or another section; null for the other kinds.

usage.description: A data item's usage, as the USAGE clause spells it, or null for a group that states none and for the other kinds.

picture.description: A data item's PICTURE character-string as written, or null.

category.description: A data item's category (ISO §2023:8.5.2): GROUP, ALPHANUMERIC, NUMERIC, NUMERIC-EDITED, NATIONAL, BOOLEAN, ...; null for the other kinds.

occursMin.description: The OCCURS clause's minimum number of occurrences, or null when the item is no table.

occursMax.description: The OCCURS clause's maximum (0 for a table of dynamic capacity), or null.

dependingOn.description: The Id of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON object, or null.

indexes.description: The Id of each index-name the item's INDEXED BY phrase declares.

redefines.description: The Id of the item a REDEFINES clause redefines, or null.

renamesFrom.description: For a level-66 entry, the Id of data-name-2, else null.

renamesThru.description: For a level-66 entry with THROUGH, the Id of data-name-3, else null.

offset.description: The offset of a data item's first occurrence from the start of its level-1 record, in bytes; null when it has no fixed offset (an item of a table of dynamic capacity), has no storage (an entry of a type declaration, a report group description entry, an implicit register) and for the other kinds.

length.description: A data item's length in character positions (the value of FUNCTION LENGTH, ISO §2023:15.50), or null.

bytes.description: The bytes a data item occupies, every occurrence of a table counted; null for an entry that has no storage and for the other kinds.

nativeField.description: The field of the compiled program that holds a data item or an index-name (for a method's LOCAL-STORAGE item, the method's local variable), or null for an item that owns no field (a level-66 alias, an entry with no storage, a LINKAGE SECTION item, whose storage is the activating element's, ISO §2023:13.7.1) and for the other kinds.

nativeType.description: The .NET type of that field, as C# spells it, or null with NativeField.

values.description: A condition-name's values as its VALUE clause writes them (a range as low THRU high), or a constant-name's specification as written, or a cd-name's FOR phrase (INPUT, OUTPUT or I-O, after INITIAL when the entry writes it); empty for the other kinds and for a refused constant entry.

typeDeclaration.description: The entry is a type declaration (a TYPEDEF entry) or part of one, or a condition-name or index-name of such an entry: it describes a type and has no storage (ISO §2023:13.18.58.4 GR2); the entries a TYPE clause copies from it are listed where that clause is written.

implicit.description: The standard defines the item implicitly where the entry that names it is written (a CAPACITY IN register, ISO §2023:13.18.38.3 SR30; an entry of a CD's record area, ISO §1985:XIV.2.2), so no data description entry of its own describes it. A compiler temporary is no declared name and is not in the data map.

files.description: Every file-name of every program, in the order written.

items.description: One file-name of the file map (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.6).

program.description: The Id of the program that declares it, or null.

line.description: The listing line of its file control entry, or null when the listing holds none.

column.description: The 1-based character position of that entry in the line's text, or null with Line.

organization.description: Its organization: SEQUENTIAL, LINE SEQUENTIAL, RELATIVE or INDEXED.

access.description: Its access mode: SEQUENTIAL, RANDOM or DYNAMIC.

records.description: The Id of each of its record descriptions.

recordKey.description: The RECORD KEY clause's key (ISO §2023:12.4.5.12), or null when the entry writes none.

name.description: The key as written: the data-name (with its subscripts), or the record-key-name a SOURCE phrase defines.

items.description: The Id of each data item the key is made of, in the order they compose it.

alternateKeys.description: Each ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause's key (ISO §2023:12.4.5.6), in the order written.

items.description: A key of an indexed file (the file map, DESIGN-listing.md section 6.6).

name.description: The key as written: the data-name (with its subscripts), or the record-key-name a SOURCE phrase defines.

items.description: The Id of each data item the key is made of, in the order they compose it.

relativeKey.description: The Id of the RELATIVE KEY data item (ISO §2023:12.4.5.13), or null.

reports.description: The Id of each report its REPORT clause names.

connector.description: The name the run unit registers the file connector under: the program's path and the file-name, the external name of an EXTERNAL file, or the class's band for a file of an object or a factory.

connectorField.description: For a file of an object or a factory, the field that holds each object's own connector key; null for every other file.

crossReference.description: The cross-reference: every declared name with its definition and its references, and the PERFORM and CALL graphs; null when the section was not asked for or could not be produced.

symbols.description: Every symbol, sorted by name (the standard's case-insensitive fold of the name) and then by the line it is defined on.

items.description: One declared name and its uses.

name.description: The name as declared (FILLER is not listed; a copy member is its text-name).

kind.description: What the name names. Program: A program-name or a user-function-name. Data: A data-name of a data description entry, a level-66 entry included. Condition: A condition-name. Index: An index-name. Constant: A constant-name. File: A file-name. Report: A report-name. CommunicationDescription: A cd-name. Procedure: A paragraph-name or a section-name. SwitchCondition: A SPECIAL-NAMES switch-status condition-name. ClassName: A class-name of a CLASS clause. Alphabet: An alphabet-name of an alphanumeric ALPHABET clause. NationalAlphabet: An alphabet-name of an ALPHABET … FOR NATIONAL clause. SymbolicCharacter: A symbolic-character. OrderingName: An ordering-name. DynamicLengthStructure: A dynamic-length-structure-name. Locale: A locale-name. Mnemonic: A mnemonic-name. ReportGroup: The data-name of a report group, as a reference that names a report group uses it. SumCounter: A sum counter. ReportVarying: A report VARYING counter. ReportEntry: A report entry named before the report section binds. ReportSumOperand: A SUM clause's data-name-1. ProgramPrototype: A program-prototype-name. ExternalProgram: A program no source element of the compilation group defines, named by the literal of a CALL or CANCEL. FunctionPrototype: A function-prototype-name. DebugRegister: The DEBUG-ITEM special register or one of its members. TypeName: A type-name. CapacityRegister: A named OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY register. ObjectClass: An object-class-name. Interface: An interface-name. ParameterName: A parameter-name of a parameterized class or interface definition. CopyMember: A library text a COPY statement names: its definition is none, each COPY statement that names it a reference.

program.description: The Id of the innermost program its definition stands in, or null.

dataItem.description: The Id of its data map entry, when the data map holds it.

references.description: Its definition (Defined, absent for a name the standard declares implicitly) and every reference, by listing line and column.

items.description: One use of a name.

line.description: The listing line it is written on, or null when no listed line holds it.

column.description: The 1-based character position of its first character in that line's text, or null.

length.description: The characters it is written in: qualifiers, subscripts and reference modification included.

use.description: How it uses the name. Defined: The declaration. Read: A reference at no position its statement stores into. Written: A reference at a position its statement stores into, wholly or in part. Modified: A reference at a position its statement reads and stores into (ADD TO, SUBTRACT FROM, INSPECT REPLACING, a STRING POINTER, ...).

verb.description: The verb of the statement it is written in, upper case (the transfer of a procedure reference: PERFORM, GO, ALTER, SORT, MERGE; the verb of a file or program reference), or null outside every statement.

unreferenced.description: The name is defined and the program never references it.

performs.description: The PERFORM graph: one edge per procedure a PERFORM statement names, from the procedure the statement is written in, in listing order.

items.description: One edge of the PERFORM or CALL graph.

from.description: The Id of the procedure (PERFORM) or source unit (CALL) the statement is written in, or null when none is defined before it.

line.description: The listing line of the reference.

verb.description: The verb of the statement, upper case.

calls.description: The CALL graph: one edge per program, function or method prototype a statement activates by name, from the source unit the statement is written in, in listing order.

items.description: One edge of the PERFORM or CALL graph.

objectCode.description: The COBOL to object-code map read from the assembly and its PDB, its instructions when the object-code section was asked for; null when neither the object-code map nor the object code was asked for, or the compilation wrote no assembly.

assembly.description: The path of the assembly the map was read from, as the compilation wrote it.

methods.description: Every method of the assembly that holds the code of a statement of the listing, in metadata order.

items.description: A method of the assembly that holds the code of statements of the listing.

token.description: The method's metadata token (ECMA-335 II.22.26, table 0x06).

type.description: The full name of the type that declares the method, a nested type after its enclosing type and a '/'.

name.description: The method's name in the metadata.

codeSize.description: The size of the method's IL body in bytes.

regions.description: The body's exception-handling clauses (ECMA-335 II.25.4.6), in the order the body lists them, which puts a clause nested in another before it (ECMA-335 I.12.4.2.7); empty for a body with none.

items.description: One exception-handling clause of a method body (ECMA-335 II.25.4.6): a protected block (its try block) and the handler that runs for it, as the body's data section holds them. Offsets are IL offsets in the method; an end is the offset after the block's last instruction.

kind.description: What kind of handler the clause has. Catch: A typed handler: it runs when the exception is an instance of the clause's type (catch). Filter: A filtered handler: the filter block decides whether the handler runs (filter). Finally: A handler that runs whenever the protected block is left (finally). Fault: A handler that runs only when the protected block is left by an exception (fault).

tryStart.description: The IL offset of the protected block's first instruction.

tryEnd.description: The IL offset after the protected block.

handlerStart.description: The IL offset of the handler's first instruction.

handlerEnd.description: The IL offset after the handler.

filterStart.description: For a Filter clause, the IL offset of its filter block's first instruction (the filter block runs to the handler's start); null for every other kind.

catchType.description: For a Catch clause, the type it catches, named as an instruction's operand names a type (Operand); null for every other kind.

ranges.description: Every stretch of a statement's object code, in listing order (by line, then column, then method and IL offset). A statement compiled more than once (a statement the compiler emits in two places) has a range for each.

items.description: One stretch of a COBOL statement's object code.

line.description: The listing line the statement begins on.

column.description: The 1-based character position of the statement's first character in that line's text.

method.description: The Id of the method holding the code.

start.description: The IL offset of the statement's sequence point.

end.description: The IL offset after the stretch: the next statement's sequence point in the method, or the end of its body.

instructions.description: The IL instructions of the stretch, in order, when the object-code section was asked for; null otherwise.

items.description: One IL instruction (ECMA-335 partition III), decoded from the method body.

offset.description: The instruction's IL offset in its method.

operand.description: The operand as text, or null for an instruction that takes none: a number, a quoted string, a branch target as IL_xxxx, a switch's targets, or the type, field or method a token names (Type::Member).

regions.description: The lines of the method's exception-handling structure the stretch prints among its instructions, in the order they print, when the object-code section was asked for; null otherwise. A line prints in the stretch whose code it bounds: a line that opens a block in the stretch holding its offset, a line that closes one in the stretch holding the block's last instruction (so a block inside one stretch opens and closes in it); one whose code no stretch of the map holds, in the method's next stretch, before its first instruction, or, when there is none, after the last instruction of the method's last stretch.

items.description: One line of a method's exception-handling structure, placed among a stretch's instructions (DESIGN-listing.md section 6.9): it prints before the instruction at Offset, or after the stretch's last instruction when no instruction of the stretch is at or after it.

offset.description: The IL offset of the boundary.

boundary.description: Which boundary the line is. TryStart: A protected block begins: .try {. Several clauses protecting the same block share one. TryEnd: A protected block ends: } // end .try. FilterStart: A filter clause's filter block begins: filter {. FilterEnd: A filter clause's filter block ends: } // end filter. HandlerStart: A handler begins: catch Type {, finally {, fault {, or a filter clause's { // handler. HandlerEnd: A handler ends: } // end handler.

region.description: The clause the boundary belongs to, as its 1-based position in Regions; for a protected block several clauses share, the first of them.

depth.description: The nesting depth of the line: 0 outside every block of the method, one more inside each block that contains the boundary.

The nesting depth (Depth) in effect at the stretch's first line, its first instruction or its first region line: the depth the method's earlier stretches leave, which is the number of the method's blocks that contain the stretch's start when the stretch before it ends there.

sections.description: Each section the listing was asked for, in the order of ListingSection: produced, or why not (DESIGN-listing.md section 4.3). A section not asked for has no entry and its part of the document is empty: the lines and the DISPLAY transfers are the source section's, the diagnostics the diagnostics section's. The header, the files, the inclusions and the programs are always present, since the lines and every page heading refer to them.

items.description: Whether a section was produced and, when not, why (DESIGN-listing.md section 4.3): a section is never left out silently.

section.description: The section. Source: The source section: every physical line of every file read, with the DISPLAY directive's transfers. Programs: The program map: every source unit, its nesting and its listing lines. Diagnostics: The diagnostics: each at its line in the source section, and all of them in the summary at the end. Options: The options in effect: every option with its value and whether it is the default, the compiler and the host. Statistics: The statistics: lines by kind and by file, programs, statements, diagnostics by severity, and each verb with its count and its lines. DataMap: The data map and the file map: every data item, condition-name, index-name, constant-name, report-name, cd-name and file-name with its level, offset, lengths, usage, picture and the .NET field it became, and each file's keys, reports and connector; and, in the source section, each data description line's offset, length and usage in the margin. CrossReference: The cross-reference: every declared name with its definition and each reference the program wrote to it, classified read, written or modified, the PERFORM and CALL graphs; and, in the source section, each line's names and a statement line's definitions in the margin. ObjectMap: The object-code map: each COBOL statement's method and IL offset range, read from the assembly the compilation wrote and its portable PDB. ObjectCode: The object code: under each COBOL statement, its IL instructions, decoded from the assembly the compilation wrote.

produced.description: Whether the listing holds the section.

reason.description: Why the section was not produced (the phase that stopped it), or null when it was.
